chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asbat ibn Salim who said:
I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he asked us about Umar ibn Muslim, what he was doing. So I said: 'He is a righteous man, but he has abandoned trade.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The work of Satan!' — (saying it) three times. 'Does he not know that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) bought a caravan of camels that came from Syria, and he gained profit from it — with which he paid off his debts and distributed among his relatives?
God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Men whom neither trade nor selling diverts from the remembrance of God' — up to the end of the verse [24:37].

The story-tellers say: These men were not merchants. They lie! Rather, they did not abandon the prayer in its prescribed time. And he (who does both) is superior to one who attends the prayer but does not trade.

key_terms.التِّجَارَة: Trade, commerce — presented here as a religious and social duty, not merely a worldly pursuit
key_terms.الْقُصَّاصُ: Story-tellers, popular preachers — used critically here for those who misinterpret Quran to discourage commerce
key_terms.عَمَلُ الشَّيْطَانِ: Work of Satan — the Imam's forceful condemnation of abandoning livelihood and commerce
key_terms.مِيقَاتِهَا: The prescribed time — refers to performing salat within its designated time window, not delaying it

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq condemn abandoning trade and commerce in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) strongly condemns the abandonment of trade and commerce, declaring it 'the work of Satan.' He cites the Prophet's own active engagement in trade — purchasing a caravan from Syria and using the proceeds to pay debts and support family — as the prophetic model to follow. The Imam also corrects a misinterpretation of Quran 24:37 by story-tellers who claimed the verse praised those who abandoned trade entirely; in reality, the verse praises those who engage in commerce while not neglecting prayer, which is a higher station than one who prays but does not work.
word_analysis: so he profited/gained surplus from it
